Smelter-acid byproduct flows may be more investable through equipment, logistics and distribution names than through headline copper/nickel miners; Teck's Trail Operations is a useful North American reference asset for this mapping.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid chokepoint with an underfollowed discovery bias. The strongest small/mid-cap discovery names are not obvious copper or nickel miners: Hawkins as a US bulk chemical distributor with explicit sulphuric-acid catalog exposure, Kirby as a domestic bulk-liquid/agricultural-chemical tank-barge logistics gatekeeper, and CECO as a niche sulphuric-acid/fertilizer mist-elimination and corrosion-control equipment supplier. Teck is included as a higher-cap reference because its Trail smelting complex manufactures sulphuric acid and liquid sulphur dioxide, making it a useful North American smelter-acid byproduct anchor. All candidates require further revenue-sensitivity verification; this is not a buy/sell list.
